s: a diminutive of the male given name Joachim, from Hebrew

a Cimbrian, one of the Cimbri (ancient tribe)
Kimber.et: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek Κίμβρος (Kímbros). Introduced to distinguish from Zimber (“speaker of a Bavarian variety in Italy”).

s: a notch, particularly in the sight of a firearm
Kimme.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German kimme (“edge; horizon”). Doublet of Kimm. Cognate with Dutch kim (“horizon”).

s: Die Kimm zeichnet sich nun ringsum schon klar und deutlich ab.
The horizon is now becoming clearly visible all around.
Kimm.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German kimme (“edge; horizon”). Doublet of Kimme. Cognate with Dutch kim (“horizon”).

Kimono.et: Borrowed from Japanese 着(き)物(もの) (kimono, “clothing”).
